title: Lipschitz-Constrained Discriminators in Generative Modeling: Asymptotic Behavior and Support Mismatch
abstract: arXiv:2611.18394v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of optimal discriminators associated to $L-$Lipschitz regularized KL-divergences of two probability distributions $Q$ and $P$ that interpolate between the rescaled Wasserstein$-1$ metric by some parameter $L>0$ and the KL divergence. The parameter $L$ plays the role of a Lipschitz constraint and is viewed as a regularization parameter: small values of $L$ enforce a more geometry-aware discriminator, while as $L$ increases the geometric regularization is progressively relaxed. It is a known result [3] that such divergences converge to the KL divergence as $L\to\infty$. tldr: 本文刻画了生成建模中带 Lipschitz 约束的最优判别器在正则化参数 $L$ 趋于无穷时的渐近行为，涵盖了绝对连续且 Radon-Nikodym 导数有界、以及离散分布等多种情形。
en_tdlr: This paper characterizes the asymptotic behavior of Lipschitz-constrained optimal discriminators in generative modeling as the regularization parameter $L$ tends to infinity, covering regimes of absolute continuity with bounded Radon-Nikodym derivatives and discrete distributions.
